requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
I found no gap against the subject's text. Each obligation has code reachable from the {impl} items and a test that carries a {test} reference.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **`habeas status` warns about items without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind and name.**
  - `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` calls `inspected_coverage_warnings`, which calls `coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`.
  - `warnings` drops items that `RecentCoverage::covers` says have recent coverage.
  - `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_section]` renders the "Coverage warnings" section.
  - Each warning line is built by `rust_coverage.rs#fn[uncovered_error]` as `<file>:<line>: <kind> <name> has no recent coverage…`.
  - `rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` is reached from `coverage_warnings` through `inspect_repository`. It collects the uncovered items.
- **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
  - `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` calls `habeas::coverage_warnings` and prints the warnings and the incomplete-history note on stderr.
  - `main` calls it after the batch summary, after a current single record is kept, and after a single authoring run.
  - It does not call it after a cancelled batch, which has not finished.
  - A failed batch still prints warnings before it returns its error.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
  - `coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_module]` handles inline `mod tests`.
  - `coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_file]` handles out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/` modules.
  - `validate_rust_functions` sets `in_tests` from both, and `warnings` filters on it.
- **A warning MUST NOT fail validation.**
  - `validate_rust_functions` pushes uncovered items to the `uncovered` list, not to `errors`.
  - A `#[test]` without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
- **Repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.** Only `coverage_history::warnings` loads Git history, and it is called only from `inspected_coverage_warnings`, not from validation.

**Tests**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]`:
  - covers a new function that is warned about at once;
  - covers `parse` becoming a warning only after the third re-authoring;
  - covers the `mod tests` fixture not being warned about;
  - covers a warning not failing validation.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` checks the status section and its file:line, kind and name format. It also checks the incomplete note on a shallow clone.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` checks that author warnings go to stderr and not to stdout.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` checks that validation is unchanged with the Git objects removed.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]` and `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` test the `tests` module exclusion.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` covers the test-versus-warning split.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs` has several tests that check author-side warnings and the incomplete-history note.

**Unspecified behavior**
The "Coverage warnings could not be computed" message in status and the stderr headings are wording for output the text requires. I treated them as specified.

`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail

:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
